timeline.phase: 1a. Rescaling dichotomy and nonseparable invariants (sec 1, p1, L17-25)
timeline.approach: Seek an intrinsic obstruction: use the Dykema-Radulescu dichotomy/absorption equivalence; try to transfer the BDIP distinction of nonseparable abelian free powers, Dykema-Zhao nonseparable rescalings, Peterson's elementary-equivalence separation.
literature_invoked: [40] Peterson, ultraproduct approximations (L(SL3 Z) vs L(F2))
timeline.why_abandoned: No mechanism transports an arbitrary separable isomorphism to the nonseparable objects; elementary equivalence does not separate rank 2 from rank 3.

timeline.phase: 1b. Rigidity, Cartan, trace-scaling flows, 1-boundedness (sec 1, p1, L26-35)
timeline.approach: Rigid free-product components; Gaussian crossed products + unique Cartan; differentiating a trace-scaling flow; strong 1-boundedness / 1-bounded entropy.
timeline.why_abandoned: Rigidity leaves an uncontrolled conjugating unitary; cannot induce isomorphism of crossed products; flow existence is equivalent to the problem (circular); 1-bounded entropy is infinite on the whole family (constant invariant).

timeline.phase: 1c. Microstate width dimension and equivariant encodings (sec 1, p1-2, L35-59)
timeline.approach: Replace Minkowski-type microstate entropy by width dimension of continuous encodings; upper bound nN^2 vs desired lower bound ~sN^2; then exploit unitary equivariance of trace-polynomial approximants; then Connes-Shlyakhtenko algebraic L2-homology.
timeline.why_abandoned: Self-constructed counterexamples: commutative rounding keeps approximate recovery while collapsing coarse dimension; tensor-twisted embeddings keep infinitely many Fourier coefficients. Continuous L2-cohomology vanishes.
timeline.verbatim_excerpt: Unknown W* invariance due bad approximations. Could try circumvent using local topological dimension/mean dimension rather than Minkowski.

timeline.phase: 2a. Nonseparable auxiliaries, free-Jacobian rank, boundary/index (sec 2, p2, L61-73)
timeline.approach: Adjoin nonseparable factors; bound free-Jacobian rank through polynomial factorization; proper proximality / free Hilbert transforms / Julg-Valette tree operator index.
timeline.why_abandoned: Reduces to separable support; derivatives uncontrolled in the limit (checkerboard counterexample); a shift on shrinking projections removes the index defect.

timeline.phase: 2b. Absorption-contradiction, automatic continuity, generators, couplings, corners (sec 2, p2-3, L74-101)
timeline.approach: Contradict Q1*Q2 = Q1*Q2*L(F_inf) using rigid components; L2-homology again; Ringrose continuity; Shen invariant; Ge-Popa; Jung; L(F_inf) copies near finite sets; Gaboriau cost/l2-Betti coupling; self-similar corners; matrix-amplification row argument; ultralimit self-inclusion.
timeline.why_abandoned: Rigidity misses the extra free part; derivations not determined by weakly dense generators; positivity unknown; L2-closeness is weaker than exact agreement on large sets; bulk errors on a trace-1/k projection give order-one row errors (recognised as the Julg-Valette obstruction); operator-norm control missing.

timeline.phase: 3a. Fock sectors, entropy-dimension iteration, Fox-derivative closability (sec 3, p3, L103-121)
timeline.approach: Extra Fock-space sectors; generalized wreath products; norm-ideal invariants; replicate an isomorphism to amplify free-entropy-dimension gap; Fox derivatives with closability in measure, filtering prefix-suffix coefficients to a diagonal subgroup; relative L2-homology.
timeline.why_abandoned: Inverse need not preserve the selected subspace; continuity moduli uncontrolled; closability missing and, even if proved, an arbitrary isomorphism's image need not lie in the domain; cycle space of dimension n-1 survives the filtering.
timeline.verbatim_excerpt: Even if prove D closable in measure, does it solve problem? Isom T arbitrary M elements not necessarily in domain.

timeline.phase: 3b. Conditional corner absorption and the fundamental-group reformulation (sec 3, p3-4, L122-151)
timeline.approach: Assuming an affirmative answer, modify corners of Q1*Q2 (Avitzour), compute pM0p = pP0p * L(F2), seek absorption of L(F_inf) through near-identity maps; then rewrite N2 = N3 as 1/sqrt2 in F(N2) via interpolation formulas.
timeline.why_abandoned: No compactness/surjectivity of the limiting map; property (T) aligns but does not control free products; Christensen-Wang complementedness blocked. The amplification reformulation is correct but circular (equivalent to the problem). The amplification calculus itself is kept and reused in the final route.

timeline.phase: 4. Embedding obstructions vs uncontrolled changes of generators (sec 4, p4-5, L153-199)
timeline.approach: Long alternating words; free shift entropy; Gibbs transport; commuting Haar witnesses giving a free triple and partition dimensions 3d vs 1+d; sweep of earlier ideas; iterate a hypothetical n->m semicircular transformation; tail permutations, Baire, Sobolev closability, graph products, max-amenable, free Stein dimension; finite Fourier-support images.
timeline.why_abandoned: An abstract isomorphism need not preserve the selected partition algebra or witnesses; iterated errors e_j <= delta_j + L_j e_{j-1} blow up with uncontrolled Lipschitz constants; Baire loses a uniform radius; closability of delta does not give closability of P delta.
timeline.verbatim_excerpt: Since f fixed measurable, L(delta) can grow without bound arbitrarily; automorphism may pathological.

timeline.approach: Matrix entries and free compression; automatic continuity again; Peterson-Thom consequences; BDIP sans-rank with Dykema-Zhao rescaling; Nielsen substitutions; absorption + IPP rigidity.
timeline.why_abandoned: Rare contractions preserve invertibility; iterative encodings need rough decoders; Nielsen substitutions mix components and destroy the commutation needed to transfer to enlargements; conjugacies do not control the free complement.

timeline.phase: 5b. Constructive turn: Ornstein-Weiss analogy, missing root on the Cayley tree (sec 5, p5-6, L221-244)
timeline.approach: Free Haar vertex variables x_g on the Cayley tree of F_d; free edge increments x_g^* x_{g s_i}; recover the missing root by giving vertex unitaries nonzero mean (classical analogy: non-uniform labels fix the global shift). Try free monotone transport to remove the resulting correlations.
timeline.why_abandoned: Generation is recovered but exact freeness is lost; transport regularity not established; a spectral-gap argument shows free generating tuples are isolated from the nearby nonfree generating sets (no Baire smoothing). Route dropped, but the 'absorb/recover a missing generator' framing persists.
timeline.verbatim_excerpt: Aha! For classical vertex labels in a group with non-uniform distribution, edge differences determine absolute labels almost surely ...

timeline.phase: 6a. Return to microstate invariants (sec 6, p6, L246-259)
timeline.approach: Generator-independent microstate invariant; Jung hyperfinite inequality; zero-entropy shifts; Urysohn width + Borsuk-Ulam spectral clipping; packing rank; ultrapower-embedding mixtures.
timeline.why_abandoned: Same closability failure; obstruction cannot be restricted uniformly to a prescribed free law; projection onto one coordinate defeats the global-negation argument.
timeline.verbatim_excerpt: Difference P(V)-U small but derivative of difference can be huge; no closability. Same old.

timeline.phase: 6b. Absorption flow and small cocycle (sec 6, p6-7, L260-292)
timeline.approach: Absorb a free generator through small perturbations. Straight cocycle paths fail; propose the polynomial flow dU_i/dt = i(sum_g h_i(g) U_g S U_g^*) U_i with a complementary semicircular S; Fox derivatives of long words with free prefixes amplify small coefficients; prefix-sum operator P = 1 + sum lambda(p_r), Q = PP^*, spectral cutoff E, h = R P^* Q^{-1} E delta_e with Ph = R E delta_e and ||h||^2 <= R^2/(dk); Haagerup bound; Catalan moments / Marchenko-Pastur limit with no atom at 0; measurable Haar reparametrization; diagonal iteration with budgets; amplification transfer from ranks 3/4 to 2/3; C*-algebra sanity check.
literature_invoked: [53] Voiculescu coalgebra of free difference quotient

timeline.phase: 7. Bounded logarithm, free-sum estimate, target correction, limiting generation (sec 7, p7-8, L293-342)
timeline.approach: Replace semicircular S by S = Arg(C) (e^{iS} = C, tau(S) = 0); free-sum bound ||sum h(g) S_g|| <= 3 pi ||h||_2 via creation/annihilation/diagonal split; trace preservation by single-variable conjugations + analytic continuation of moments; correct target from C to C A_w and invert by a Nielsen automorphism; summable perturbations; separate L2-density argument for generation; consistency checks (cyclomorphy, BDIP, Weyl-von Neumann vs index, Mei-Ricard, relative freeness, analytic radius); amplification to ranks 2/3.

lesson.obstruction: BDIP's invariant (the 'sans-rank') separates A^{*n} only for NONSEPARABLE diffuse abelian A. It relies on uncountable cardinality and has no separable analogue. Dykema-Zhao rescalings of free products with nonseparable abelian parts leave the nonseparable component count unchanged when the separable free-group parameter changes. A separable isomorphism L(F2)=L(F3) gives no isomorphism between the enlarged nonseparable objects. Peterson's elementary-equivalence separation applies to L(SL3 Z) vs L(F2) (property-T phenomena), not between free group factors.
lesson.lesson_statement: Nonseparable invariants cannot be used, because no functor carries an arbitrary separable isomorphism to the nonseparable enlargement (C1). Elementary equivalence, as used by Peterson, does not see rank.
lesson.lesson_form: negative result + constraint on future approaches
lesson.generality: general (rules out the class: invariants of nonseparable enlargements unless the enlargement is functorial in the isomorphism)
lesson.known_in_literature: Known: BDIP (GAFA 2024) present their theorem as a nonseparable analogue and do not claim a separable consequence; Dykema-Zhao (JFA 2026) discuss it. The elementary-equivalence status of free group factors is studied by Goldbring-Pi (arXiv:2305.08168, cited in the paper, not the trace).
lesson.salvage: none (the BDIP/Dykema-Zhao rescaling formulas reappear only as consistency checks at L323-325)
lesson.influence: contributory to the NEG exhaustion; weak as pruning, since the same idea is re-tried 6 more times (L62, L104, L156, L211, L250, L323)
lesson.what_was_not_learned: The model did not conclude once and for all that the separable-to-nonseparable transport is impossible in principle (if L(F2)=L(F3), the enlargements are presumably still distinguished by BDIP, so no contradiction can arise). It relearned the clause repeatedly.

nodes.description: Rigid free-product components / Gaussian crossed products

lesson.obstruction: Both variants need structure that an abstract isomorphism does not supply: a controlled conjugacy (a2.1) or a group action (a2.2).
lesson.lesson_statement: Rigidity and crossed-product methods do not transport through an arbitrary isomorphism (C2; a precursor of C14).
lesson.known_in_literature: Known (deformation/rigidity has never separated free group factors)
lesson.what_was_not_learned: C14 is not yet stated in general form.

nodes.description: Rigidity of components to expose extra free directions (Popa; free-group-factor dichotomy, many semicirculars)

lesson.obstruction: Deformation/rigidity (Popa; Ioana-Peterson-Popa) locates rigid subalgebras up to unitary conjugacy: intertwining gives u with u Q u* inside a component. The extra free directions of L(F3) over L(F2) live in the malleable part, which rigidity does not detect. The conjugating unitary is uncontrolled and 'might encode the extra free directions'.
lesson.lesson_statement: Rigidity arguments cannot see the soft free part; they leave an uncontrolled conjugating unitary (C2).
lesson.known_in_literature: Known barrier: free group factors are s-malleable and have no rigid diffuse subalgebras with relative property (T). Deformation/rigidity theory has never distinguished L(F_n)s (Popa ICM surveys; Ioana-Peterson-Popa, Acta 2008).
lesson.influence: contributory (reapplied at a10 L77, a18.2 L133, a29 L219-220)

nodes.description: Gaussian crossed product + Popa-Vaes unique Cartan

lesson.obstruction: Popa-Vaes unique Cartan applies to L-infinity(X) crossed with F_n. A Gaussian action needs the group F_n and an orthogonal representation, not just the von Neumann algebra L(F_n). An abstract isomorphism L(F2)=L(F3) does not induce an isomorphism of the crossed products.
lesson.lesson_statement: Constructions that use the group structure (crossed products) cannot be induced by an abstract algebra isomorphism.
lesson.known_in_literature: Known (Popa-Vaes, Acta 2014; standard remark that W*-invariants must not use the group).
lesson.what_was_not_learned: Did not yet state the general clause C14; that happens at a15 (L104-105).

nodes.description: Differentiate a trace-scaling flow

lesson.obstruction: Chakraborty-Novac (arXiv:2608.15385) tie the existence of a continuous trace-scaling flow on the stabilisation of L(F2) to whether its fundamental group is all of R+. That holds iff the free group factors are isomorphic, given the dichotomy F(L(F_r)) in {R+, {1}}.
lesson.lesson_statement: Differentiating a trace-scaling flow is circular, since such a flow exists only if the answer is already affirmative (C3).
lesson.known_in_literature: Known: Radulescu (1992) built such a flow for L(F_inf) tensor B(H); Chakraborty-Novac 2026.
lesson.correctness: correct. In hindsight it is an affirmative signpost: the final paper's corollary gives F(L(F2)) = R+.
lesson.what_was_not_learned: The model did not read circularity as weak evidence for the affirmative answer.

nodes.description: Strong 1-boundedness / 1-bounded entropy

lesson.obstruction: Jung strong 1-boundedness separates s1b algebras (e.g. property T, nonprime) from free group factors, but every L(F_n) is not s1b. Hayes 1-bounded entropy is infinite for all of them.
lesson.lesson_statement: Invariants that separate free group factors from other factors are constant on the family (C4).
lesson.generality: general (rules out every invariant of the 1-bounded type)
lesson.known_in_literature: Known: Jung GAFA 2007; Hayes IMRN 2018.

nodes.description: Generator-dependent microstate entropy -> width dimension

lesson.obstruction: Microstate entropy has unknown W*-invariance; width dimension has no probabilistic lower bound (rounding); equivariance does not cut the parameter count.
lesson.lesson_statement: Microstate-dimension invariants of the Minkowski or width type cannot be made generator-independent with available tools (C5a, C5, C6).
lesson.known_in_literature: Known open problem (Voiculescu invariance). The final paper proves non-invariance of delta, delta_0, delta*, delta^star.
lesson.what_was_not_learned: Not carried into sec 6a: the width line is restarted from scratch at c3.

nodes.description: Minkowski-type microstate entropy

lesson.obstruction: Microstate free entropy (dimension) is generator-dependent. W*-invariance is Voiculescu's open problem. Polynomial approximations of new generators in old ones are only L2-close ("bad approximations"), so microstate spaces cannot be transported.
lesson.lesson_statement: Minkowski-type microstate dimension cannot be shown W*-invariant (C5a); switch to topological/mean/width dimension.
lesson.verbatim_excerpt: Unknown W* invariance due bad approximations. Could try circumvent using local topological dimension/mean dimension rather than Minkowski.
lesson.known_in_literature: Known open problem (Voiculescu, Free entropy survey 2002, sec 2.6, cited in the paper). The final paper proves the NON-invariance (Cor. cor:entropy-dimensions).
lesson.correctness: correct as a statement of ignorance. If the final paper is right, the invariance it hoped for is false.
lesson.influence: decisive for the immediate sibling a5.2 (verbatim proposal of width/mean dimension)
lesson.what_was_not_learned: Did not infer that, if invariance fails, the generator-recovery map underlying an affirmative answer might exist. That reading surfaces only at L221.

nodes.description: Width dimension: upper bound nN^2 vs required lower bound ~sN^2

lesson.obstruction: Suppose s free semicirculars are recoverable from n<s generators. Polynomial approximation then gives a width upper bound nN^2 for NxN microstates, and a contradiction needs a lower bound ~sN^2 under stringent moment constraints. A commutative rounding example keeps approximate recovery while sharply reducing coarse dimension. Finite-quotient models lose too many parameters. High-probability (concentration) statements therefore do not give width lower bounds.
lesson.lesson_statement: The width lower bound cannot come from probability alone, because rounding cheats (C5).
lesson.lesson_form: negative result + sharpened target (the missing piece is exactly a uniform width lower bound)
lesson.known_in_literature: Apparently new in this setting; it is analogous to the known gap between measure-theoretic and topological dimension (Gromov waist/width).
lesson.correctness: plausible; the counterexample is described too tersely to check
lesson.influence: decisive for sibling a5.3 (equivariance proposed to rule out rounding)

nodes.description: Exploit unitary equivariance of trace-polynomial approximants

lesson.obstruction: Trace-polynomial approximants are unitarily equivariant with N-independent degree, which rules out entrywise rounding. But tensor-twisted embeddings preserve free distributions while retaining infinitely many Fourier coefficients, so the parameter count still fails.
lesson.lesson_statement: Equivariance does not restrict the effective parameter count (C6).
lesson.verbatim_excerpt: Crucially P,Q are unitarily equivariant trace-polynomial approximants with degree independent of N. Entrywise rounding isn't implementable by polynomial operations (coordinate-dependent).
lesson.known_in_literature: apparently new (unverifiable)
lesson.influence: none visible (width ideas resurface at c3 L254-256, where the lesson is not cited)
lesson.what_was_not_learned: The width line is re-entered at c3 without reference to C5/C6.

nodes.description: Algebraic L2-homology (Connes-Shlyakhtenko) vs continuous vanishing (Popa-Vaes)
explicit_time_or_compute_markers: L57: leaves the width lower bound unresolved

lesson.obstruction: Connes-Shlyakhtenko L2-Betti numbers of the group algebra C[F_n] give n-1, but they are defined for a dense *-subalgebra and their W*-invariance is open. Popa-Vaes (IMRN 2015) show that the continuous first L2-cohomology vanishes for every II1 factor, so the W*-continuous variant cannot distinguish.
lesson.lesson_statement: Generator-independent (continuous) L2-cohomology is constant (zero), and the algebraic version is not known to be invariant (C7).
lesson.known_in_literature: Known barrier (Connes-Shlyakhtenko 2005 raise the invariance question; Popa-Vaes 2015; Thom 2008).
lesson.influence: contributory (reapplied at a7, a10, a17.1, a28, c1)

nodes.description: Adjoin nonseparable auxiliary factors; derivations on restricted domains
explicit_time_or_compute_markers: L60: section title: 'the recurring boundary obstruction'

lesson.obstruction: Extensions by nonseparable auxiliary factors reduce to a separable support algebra; BDIP again cannot be transported. Popa-Vaes vanishing prompts derivations on restricted domains.
lesson.lesson_statement: Nonseparable auxiliaries collapse to separable data (C1 again).
lesson.known_in_literature: Known (as a1).
lesson.what_was_not_learned: Repetition of C1, not used as a prune.

nodes.description: Free-Jacobian rank via factoring polynomial approximations through fewer variables

lesson.obstruction: Factoring polynomial approximations through fewer variables bounds the free-Jacobian rank, but derivatives are not controlled in the limit. A commutative checkerboard example shows that strong convergence of bounded kernels need not preserve module rank, and gradient relations give no uniform estimate.
lesson.lesson_statement: Jacobian/derivative ranks do not survive approximation without derivative control (C8).
lesson.lesson_form: negative result + constraint on future approaches
lesson.generality: general (any argument that differentiates approximate generator changes)
lesson.known_in_literature: Known in spirit: rank bounds for non-microstates free entropy dimension hold for polynomials or regular functions, not for W*-functions (Shlyakhtenko; Charlesworth-Shlyakhtenko 2016; Mai-Speicher-Weber).
lesson.influence: DECISIVE for the final design: the final route avoids differentiating residuals (L283-284, "keep residuals small without differentiating them") and uses operator-norm estimates (L297-304). Relearned at c1 (L248).
lesson.what_was_not_learned: The positive form ("design a construction whose error control never differentiates") is reached only at L283.

nodes.description: Boundary approach: proper proximality, free Hilbert transforms, Julg-Valette index

lesson.obstruction: Free groups are properly proximal; Mei-Ricard free Hilbert transforms give regularity; the Julg-Valette tree operator gives a Fredholm-type index for maps L2(M) -> L2(M)^r with weakly compact commutators. A shift on normalized vectors supported on shrinking orthogonal projections removes the index defect and preserves regularity: in a II1 factor, small projections absorb integer defects.
lesson.lesson_statement: Index or K-theoretic defects are not W*-stable (C9).
lesson.generality: general (rules out index/K-theory-type invariants at the von Neumann level)
lesson.known_in_literature: Known folklore: K-theoretic distinctions of C*_r(F_n) (Pimsner-Voiculescu K1 = Z^n) do not pass to the II1 closure, where Breuer index is real-valued.
lesson.salvage: the Julg-Valette picture is re-recognised at L98 and L180; used positively as a consistency check at L327-329 (Weyl-von Neumann absorption)
lesson.influence: contributory (pruning at a13 and a23; verification at d1.3.6). Its mirror image C21 (norm-continuous constructions ARE constrained by C*-invariants) is decisive for d1.3.

nodes.description: Contradict absorption Q1*Q2 = Q1*Q2*L(F_inf) with rigid components; L2-homology again
explicit_time_or_compute_markers: L78: Returning to algebraic L2-homology

lesson.obstruction: Under an affirmative answer, Dykema-Radulescu give Q1*Q2 = Q1*Q2*L(F_inf) for all II1 factors Q1, Q2. Ioana-Peterson-Popa rigidity tracks rigid components but not the added free part. Algebraic L2-homology meets derivations not determined by weakly dense generators.
lesson.lesson_statement: Absorption with rigid components gives no contradiction; derivations are not determined on dense generators (C10).
lesson.known_in_literature: Known (Dykema-Radulescu 2003; IPP 2008; the domain problem is standard).

nodes.description: Ringrose automatic continuity; Shen generator invariant; Ge-Popa; Jung back-and-forth

lesson.obstruction: Ringrose's automatic continuity needs Banach-bimodule targets, not affiliated (unbounded) ones. Shen's generator invariant G(M) scales as t^{-2} under amplification (Dykema-Sinclair-Smith-White), but its positivity for free group factors is unknown. Ge-Popa blocks a finite-generation shortcut, and Jung's characterisation of amenability by embeddings into R^omega limits back-and-forth.
lesson.lesson_statement: Generator-number invariants lack a positive lower bound (C11); automatic continuity fails for affiliated targets.
lesson.known_in_literature: Known (Shen 2009; DSSW 2008 explicitly state the positivity question; Jung 2007).

nodes.description: L(F_inf) copies near finite sets; Gaboriau cost / l2-Betti coupling

lesson.obstruction: The idea was to place copies of L(F_inf) near finite sets. Adjoining missing coordinates imposes conjugacy relations, and spectral gap obstructs perturbing them into free bases. Gaboriau cost and measure-equivalence invariance of l2-Betti numbers rely on measurable relabeling that is EXACT on large sets, whereas operator approximations are only L2-close.
lesson.lesson_statement: Operator approximations give only L2-closeness, not exact agreement on large sets (C12).
lesson.lesson_form: negative result + sharpened target (the missing step is identified explicitly)
lesson.known_in_literature: Known (the absence of a cost invariant for II1 factors is a standard open theme; Shlyakhtenko on free entropy and cost).
lesson.salvage: The spectral-gap obstruction to perturbing into free bases foreshadows C19 (b1.4).

nodes.description: Self-similar corners; matrix-amplification distinguished row (Wick first-letter stripping)
explicit_time_or_compute_markers: L94: A matrix-amplification attempt
L98: it recognizes the earlier Julg-Valette obstruction

lesson.obstruction: Dykema's compression formula suggests self-similar corners, but identifying a corner with the original factor requires generator collapse, which is circular. In the matrix-amplification row argument, stripping the first letter of a Wick expansion has bounded total L2 norm. But bulk errors on a projection of trace ~1/k give order-one row errors, and the row space L2(M) minus C is the Julg-Valette setting again.
lesson.lesson_statement: Shrinking corners consume recovery information and rescaling magnifies errors by 1/t (C13); the row argument is the Julg-Valette obstruction (C9).
lesson.known_in_literature: Known (the amplification formula is precisely why rank comparisons reduce to corner sizes).
lesson.salvage: Wick first-letter stripping and prefix structure foreshadow the Fox-cocycle prefix sums (d1.2.1); analyst inference.

nodes.description: Ultralimit of bulk-matching automorphisms: module maps properly into itself
explicit_time_or_compute_markers: L99: Finally, it tries matching bulk embeddings
L100: It leaves open the required operator-norm control

lesson.obstruction: Matching bulk embeddings by automorphisms and passing to an ultralimit should give a module mapping properly into itself, but the operator-norm control needed for a contradiction is missing.
lesson.lesson_statement: Ultralimit self-inclusion needs operator-norm control that is unavailable.
lesson.known_in_literature: apparently new (unverifiable)

nodes.description: Fock-space extra sectors; wreath-product superrigidity; norm-ideal invariants

lesson.obstruction: Fock-space constructions give extra representation sectors, but the inverse transformation need not preserve the selected subspace. BDIP would need the isomorphism to preserve enlarged components. The Ioana-Popa-Vaes superrigidity of generalized wreath products needs specific group bases, not arbitrary free bases. Voiculescu's norm-ideal (quasicentral modulus) invariants are destroyed by rough generator changes.
lesson.lesson_statement: An abstract isomorphism need not preserve ANY auxiliary structure used to build an invariant (C14).
lesson.generality: general: rules out every presentation-dependent invariant
lesson.known_in_literature: Known: this is why generator-independence is the crux (Voiculescu's invariance problem for delta; Connes-Shlyakhtenko).
lesson.influence: DECISIVE: it is reapplied at a17.3, a22 (verbatim), a29, and it is the stated content of the shift to constructive changes of generators (L197-199, L201-202).

nodes.description: Replicate a hypothetical isomorphism to amplify the free-entropy-dimension gap

lesson.obstruction: Replicating a hypothetical isomorphism preserves its free-entropy-dimension ratio; iteration raises reconstruction complexity together with the gap. Continuity moduli are uncontrolled and Fock-space compactness is not preserved. Coordinatewise quantization blocks the step from large microstate packing numbers to a topological obstruction.
lesson.lesson_statement: Amplifying a dimension gap by iteration fails because the maps are not uniformly continuous.
lesson.known_in_literature: apparently new formulation; uses known tools
lesson.salvage: The idea of iterating a generator-changing map returns at a24 and, inverted, in the final iteration (d1.2.2).

nodes.description: Fox derivatives as an obstruction (closability, filtering)

lesson.obstruction: Fox derivatives cannot be made into an invariant: closability is unavailable (a17.1), filtering leaves an (n-1)-dimensional cycle space (a17.2), the domain does not contain images of an arbitrary isomorphism (a17.3), and relative homology gives nothing (a17.4).
lesson.lesson_statement: Fox derivatives fail as an OBSTRUCTION, but their prefix-suffix calculus is a usable tool (C15).
lesson.known_in_literature: Fox calculus is classical (Fox, Annals 1953, cited by the paper but not the trace); its closability issues are known (Thom; Alekseev-Kyed)
lesson.salvage: Cocycle rule D_gb = D_g + lambda(g) D_b and prefix sums: paper eq:flow-cocycle, Lemma lem:cocycle-prefixes (d1.2.1, L272-279)
lesson.influence: contributory to the core lemma (tool, not idea)
lesson.what_was_not_learned: The constructive use (amplifying small coefficients along many free prefixes) is not seen here.

nodes.description: Closability via Thom / Alekseev-Kyed / Popa-Vaes

lesson.obstruction: Fox derivatives on L(F_n) with affiliated values: closability would need Thom's affiliated L2-cohomology, Alekseev-Kyed measure-continuity or Popa-Vaes, and none gives the required closability.
lesson.lesson_statement: No closability statement is available for the Fox derivations.
lesson.known_in_literature: Known (closability of free difference quotients is understood for semicircular generators, not after arbitrary changes of generators).
lesson.salvage: Fox derivatives retained as a tool (C15)

nodes.description: Filter prefix-suffix coefficients onto a diagonal subgroup
nodes.conflict: other (residual cycle space of dimension n-1)

lesson.obstruction: Filtering derivative limits onto a diagonal subgroup leaves a cycle space of dimension n-1, so no vanishing relation strong enough to compare generator counts appears.
lesson.lesson_statement: Filtering leaves an (n-1)-dimensional residue (cf. b1^(2)(F_n) = n-1), so there is no rank contradiction.
lesson.known_in_literature: Consistent with known l2-Betti number b1^(2)(F_n) = n-1
lesson.salvage: The prefix-suffix structure of Fox derivatives (C15) is salvaged and becomes the cocycle rule D_gb = D_g + lambda(g) D_b (paper eq:flow-cocycle).
lesson.what_was_not_learned: The model did not notice here that the same prefix structure could AMPLIFY coefficients constructively (rather than obstruct); that took ~40% more of the trace.

nodes.description: Domain obstacle: images of an arbitrary isomorphism need not lie in the domain

lesson.obstruction: Even a closable derivation would not settle the problem, because an arbitrary isomorphism's images need not lie in the domain.
lesson.lesson_statement: Closability is insufficient because of the domain obstacle (C10, C14).
lesson.verbatim_excerpt: Even if prove D closable in measure, does it solve problem? Isom T arbitrary M elements not necessarily in domain.
lesson.known_in_literature: Known (standard).

nodes.description: Relative L2-homology over a hyperfinite subfactor (Bermudez)

lesson.obstruction: Bermudez's relative L2-homology over a hyperfinite subfactor gives no distinction the model can establish.
lesson.lesson_statement: Relative L2-homology is not computable or invariant here.
lesson.known_in_literature: Known open status

nodes.description: Conditional corner absorption under an affirmative hypothesis (seek contradiction)

lesson.obstruction: Assuming the affirmative answer gives computable corner formulas (pM0p = pP0p * L(F2)), but no contradiction: absorption maps lack compactness or surjectivity, entropy bounds and property (T) do not control free products, and complementedness is blocked.
lesson.lesson_statement: Consequences of an affirmative answer are self-consistent as far as the model can see. This is weak evidence FOR the affirmative, though the model does not read it that way.
lesson.known_in_literature: apparently new computations built on known formulas (Dykema-Radulescu; Avitzour)
lesson.salvage: absorption through near-identity maps (a18.2) -> final absorption scheme (inferred)
lesson.what_was_not_learned: The model did not reverse the direction here, which would mean trying to build the absorbing maps rather than refuting them.

nodes.description: Modify corners of Q1*Q2; Avitzour factoriality; pM0p = pP0p * L(F2)
Absorb L(F_inf) through near-identity maps fixing P0; property (T)

lesson.obstruction: Under the affirmative hypothesis, the plan was to absorb L(F_inf) through maps fixing P0 that approximate the identity uniformly on each component's unit ball. Preimages have no compactness and the limit map is not known to be surjective. Property (T) aligns components without controlling their free product. Dykema-Radulescu compression/absorption informs the construction.
lesson.lesson_statement: Approximate-identity absorption lacks compactness and surjectivity; property (T) controls components, not their free product.
lesson.lesson_form: negative result + salvaged idea (absorption through near-identity maps)
lesson.known_in_literature: apparently new formulation
lesson.salvage: The pattern "absorb an extra free piece through near-identity maps and pass to a limit" is exactly the shape of the final route (d1, d1.3.4-5), there applied constructively and with exact automorphisms. This is analyst inference; the summary draws no link.
lesson.what_was_not_learned: Not recognised as usable in the AFFIRMATIVE direction until sec 6b.

nodes.description: Jung / Jung-Shlyakhtenko bounds for free-product generators

lesson.obstruction: Jung strong 1-boundedness and the Jung-Shlyakhtenko property-(T) bound (delta_0 <= 1 for property-T generators) do not control arbitrary free-product generators.
lesson.lesson_statement: Entropy bounds do not control free-product generators.
lesson.known_in_literature: Known

nodes.description: Christensen-Wang complemented-subspace route

lesson.obstruction: The Christensen-Wang complemented-subspace route is rejected because the required complementedness is obstructed by an expected copy of L(F_inf).
lesson.lesson_statement: Complementedness is obstructed.
lesson.known_in_literature: Known in spirit (Christensen-Wang 2013)

nodes.description: Reformulate via interpolation: N2=N3 iff 1/sqrt2 in F(N2); asymptotic freeness in conditional construction
explicit_time_or_compute_markers: L149: continuing reduced-word calculations without obtaining an isomorphism or contradiction

lesson.obstruction: The interpolation formulas give N_r^t = N_{1+(r-1)/t^2} and N_r*N_s = N_{r+s}. With t = 1/sqrt2, N_2^{1/sqrt2} = N_3, so N2 = N3 iff 1/sqrt2 lies in F(N2). This is a correct reformulation, equivalent to the problem. The asymptotic-freeness investigation of the conditional construction gave no result.
lesson.lesson_statement: The problem is equivalent to fundamental-group membership; the reformulation does not decide it (C16).
lesson.lesson_form: reformulation of the problem + salvaged tool (amplification calculus)
lesson.known_in_literature: Known (Dykema 1994; Radulescu 1994; standard).
lesson.salvage: The amplification calculus is carried forward and used for the final step: the rank-3/4 isomorphism is transferred to ranks 2/3 (L288-289, L336-339; paper sec "Amplification to rank two").
lesson.influence: DECISIVE for the last step of the final proof
lesson.what_was_not_learned: The model did not see here that ANY two distinct finite ranks would suffice (consecutive ranks n, n+1 with n>=3). That realisation is implicit at L288-289.

nodes.description: Long alternating words vs component ultrapowers; nonseparable intertwining; deformation embeddings

lesson.obstruction: Long alternating words with nonperiodic letters conjugate W*(a,b^2) freely away from the component ultrapowers, which defeats the intended embedding obstruction. The cancellation bound depended on syllable length rather than on the letters, with the outer letter orthogonal to the smaller algebra.
lesson.lesson_statement: Free products let you conjugate subalgebras away from ultrapowers, so this embedding obstruction is void.
lesson.known_in_literature: Related to known asymptotic-orthogonality phenomena in free products (Popa 1983; Popa 2014 on independence in ultraproducts)
lesson.salvage: "Long alternating words" foreshadow the long prefix words of d1.2.1 (inference)

nodes.description: Free shift vs its square (entropy); Gibbs transport; hiding directions on small supports

lesson.obstruction: A free shift conjugated to its square shows no entropy distinction (Brown-Dykema-Shlyakhtenko); Gibbs/free monotone transport preserves the number of variables; supported semicirculars suggest hiding directions on small supports.
lesson.lesson_statement: Transport and entropy of shifts cannot change or detect the number of variables.
lesson.known_in_literature: Known (Guionnet-Shlyakhtenko 2014 give isomorphisms W*(X_1..X_n) = L(F_n) with the same n)
lesson.salvage: "hiding directions on small supports" foreshadows absorption (inference)

nodes.description: Commuting Haar witnesses -> free triple b, c1 b c1*, c2 b c2*; partition dimensions 3d vs 1+d

lesson.obstruction: Commuting Haar witnesses c1, c2, free from b, give the free triple b, c1 b c1*, c2 b c2*. Free dimension compares partition dimensions 3d and 1+d with d = 1 - sum t_j^2 and 1/2 < d < 2/3, which suggests room in rank two. But an abstract isomorphism need not preserve the partition algebra or the witnesses, and the embeddings are nonstandard.
lesson.lesson_statement: Free-dimension counts depend on the embedding; an isomorphism need not preserve witnesses (C14).
lesson.verbatim_excerpt: Joint law free P, embeddings not approximately conjugate. Already nonstandard vs standard yields.
lesson.known_in_literature: Known (Dykema 1993: standard vs nonstandard embeddings).
lesson.salvage: The device of free conjugates of a fixed variable by Haar unitaries (b, c b c*) reappears as S_g = A_g S A_g^* in the final flow (L262-271; paper Lemma lem:conjugates). This is analyst inference; the summary draws no link.

nodes.description: Sweep of earlier routes (survey, interpolation, absorption, rescaling, Jacobians, cohomology, s1b, cost, trace scaling, Shen, Fock rows, Hilbert transforms)
nodes.conflict: other (each blocked by an earlier learned clause)
explicit_time_or_compute_markers: L171: The assistant revisited the problem survey [47], interpolation [18, 44], absorption equivalence [16], and nonseparable rescaling [17]
L180: the tree operator returned it to the failed index approach

lesson.obstruction: A sweep of previously tried routes (survey, interpolation, absorption, rescaling, Jacobians, cohomology, s1b, cost, trace scaling, Shen, Fock rows, Hilbert transforms). Each is blocked by an earlier clause.
lesson.lesson_statement: All known invariants are blocked; the open requirement is control of arbitrary generator changes without quantitative regularity.
lesson.known_in_literature: n/a

nodes.description: Iterate a hypothetical n->m semicircular transformation; free subgroup words; orbital entropy
